capabilities.name: Multi-document ingestion with file-type checks, limits and hashing
capabilities.note: PDF, PNG and JPEG by their first bytes. By default 10 MB, 20 pages and 10 documents per case. Files are stored under their sha256; a rejected file becomes a limitation with a reason.

capabilities.name: Document classification
capabilities.note: Rules over words and layout. Three types have a spec at this build (bank statement, payslip, loan application), one drawn layout each; anything else is 'unknown' and says so. Wording that differs from the specs' may also read as 'unknown'. A local-model fallback is not built.

capabilities.name: Text-layer reading and OCR (offline)
capabilities.note: Every word has a box in page pixels. Scanned pages get a quality class from sharpness, not from the recogniser's score; numbers read from a degraded or poor page are flagged, not trusted. OCR output is a reading, not ground truth.

capabilities.name: Structured extraction: fields and tables, each with a confidence and a location
capabilities.note: Bank statements (digital and scanned), payslips and loan applications (digital so far), one drawn layout each. A column or label that is not found is reported as missing, never filled in. A deduction beside an empty earnings cell is not read as a row. Other document types and layouts are not built.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: comparison of saved revisions
capabilities.note: Text that differs between a PDF's earlier saved version and a later one is reported as an observation, with the old and the new text. The other digital checks are in the next row.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: covered and hidden text, pictures over text, fonts, file metadata
capabilities.note: Reported as observations with the measured values: text still in the file but drawn under a filled rectangle or a picture that comes after it (the text written over a covering rectangle is cited too); a figure or date set in a different font, size or colour from the others in its column or on its line; text that is invisible, under 2 pt or off the page; a producer or creator that names PDF-editing software; a modification date later than the creation date. Built against synthetic manipulations D2 to D5 and not yet evaluated on a held-out set. Not built: text hidden by its colour, covers that are not rectangles, bold against regular.

capabilities.name: Scan and image forensics
capabilities.note: Scanned words whose image grain differs from the page median are shown as observations, on pages that are not of poor quality. The check of text lines (baseline and height) is planned. How often these checks find a changed scan is measured by the evaluation, not by the tests.

capabilities.name: Checks within one document
capabilities.note: Bank statement balance chain and dates; payslip totals, net pay against its words, and pay date against pay month; the weekday printed on a loan application. Each states its tolerance. A conflict resting on a doubtful reading is shown as a possible extraction error.

capabilities.name: Cross-document conflict checks
capabilities.note: Name, address, employer and account number across documents; net pay against the credits on a statement; declared income against gross earnings; the application date against the dates of the other documents; a file submitted twice; the same producing software on different kinds of document made minutes apart. A comparison that cannot be made is reported as a limitation, never as a pass. Built for three document types with one drawn layout each, and not yet evaluated on a held-out set. Each finding prints its tolerance.

capabilities.name: Context rules (income, obligations, date windows)
capabilities.note: Two rules: monthly obligations (existing instalments plus the new loan over its tenure) as a share of declared income, and a document dated more than 90 days before the application. Both are observations for the reviewer, never conflicts. Their reference limits are synthetic values chosen for this prototype, not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest. Rules taken from a lender's own policy are not built.

capabilities.name: Relationships between findings (clusters)
capabilities.note: Findings are listed one by one; they are not yet grouped by shared evidence.

capabilities.name: Plain-language explanations and next steps from fixed templates
capabilities.note: Fixed wording per detector and class. Nothing is written by a model.

capabilities.name: Explanation wording from a local language model
capabilities.note: Not built. If added, it would only reword structured findings, and the output would be labelled as inference.

capabilities.name: Evidence traceability: finding to file, sha256, page and box, with a marked crop
capabilities.note: Every piece of evidence names its document, page and box; the trace command prints them and checks the stored file's hash.

capabilities.name: Investigation dossier: HTML (self-contained) and JSON, with its own hash
capabilities.note: Observations, inconsistencies, potential-manipulation candidates and limitations are kept in separate places.

capabilities.name: Dossier export as PDF
capabilities.note: Print the HTML dossier to PDF from a browser meanwhile.

capabilities.name: Tamper-evident audit trail with a verify command
capabilities.note: Each event carries the hash of the one before it. The dossier records the trail's length and last hash.

capabilities.name: Safe failure: rejected files, failed or stuck steps become visible limitations
capabilities.note: A step that fails or times out is listed as a limitation and the case goes on. A step stuck in native code is abandoned, not killed.

capabilities.name: Offline operation
capabilities.note: The OCR models ship inside the package. The test suite runs with connections to public addresses blocked.

capabilities.name: Review interface in the browser
capabilities.note: Runs on this computer only. Upload, a background run with progress, page images with word, field and finding boxes, evidence crops, reviewer actions written to the audit trail, the audit trail, this list and the dossier download. The server side is tested; how the page behaves in a browser was checked by hand, not by an automated browser test. Findings are not yet grouped into clusters, so that tab is empty.

capabilities.name: Handwriting and multilingual OCR
capabilities.note: Not built; text is read as printed English.

capabilities.name: Real-world document layouts at scale
capabilities.note: Only synthetic documents were used. Nothing is claimed about real ones.

capabilities.name: Verdicts on authenticity or intent; verification of signatures and identity documents
capabilities.note: Unsupported by design. The tool lists anomalies for a human reviewer and never concludes.

limitations: Every document used to build and test this tool is synthetic. Nothing was evaluated on real documents, real scanners or real layouts.
Findings are for a human reviewer. An ordinary cause (a re-issue, a rounding rule, a misread digit, an unusual layout) can produce any of them, and the tool cannot tell which.
OCR output is a reading, not ground truth. On scans a number from a degraded or poor page is not trusted, and a conflict that rests on one is shown as a possible extraction error.

The statement checks assume the oldest row comes first and that a balance follows each row. A statement listed newest first, or with signed amounts, is reported as a layout the checks do not assume and is not checked.
A totals row at the foot of a statement is not read, so it is not checked.
A transaction row that extraction misses (for example one with a garbled date on a scan) shows up as a balance break at the next row.

The saved-revision comparison reads incremental saves only. By default a linearized PDF is not compared, at most 16 revisions of a file are opened and a page of more than 5000 words is not compared; each of these is reported as a limitation.
A PDF that was saved more than once for an ordinary reason (a correction, a re-issue, a form being filled in) shows revision observations too.

The cover check looks at opaque rectangular fills, and at pictures smaller than half a page, drawn after the text they lie over. A cover of another form (a curve, a clipped path), text hidden by its colour, and the draw order of a picture on a file whose page content is unusual are not handled; a page that draws more than 5000 objects is not examined and the dossier says so. Invisible text on a page that is mostly one picture is taken as the text layer of a scan and is not reported.

The font check compares figures and dates that stand in a text run of their own with the others in their column (four or more) or on their line (three or more). A figure inside a longer run of text is not compared, and bold against regular of one family is not. A logo, stamp or signature placed as a picture on a text page is reported like any other picture.

The metadata check reads what the file says about itself: producer and creator names, creation and modification dates. Anyone who can write the file can write them, and a file saved again for an ordinary reason shows a later modification date.

The grain check compares each scanned word with the median of its page, on the paper inside the word's box and away from the ink, and leaves out paper brighter than 250 (the scanner cuts it at white). Scanners and JPEG saves change grain for ordinary reasons. On a mildly degraded scan a changed word can keep a grain close to the page's, because the second JPEG save puts back grain of about the same size, so the check finds a patch more easily on coarser scans. Pages of poor quality are not analysed and the dossier says so.

A revision boundary is recognised from a startxref pointer followed by %%EOF. A file crafted to carry a convincing pointer inside a content stream can mislead it, which gives a false observation or a visible limitation, not a silent pass.

A document the tool does not recognise as one of the three supported types is left out of the comparisons across documents, and the dossier says which comparisons were not made. Wording unlike the specs' can read as unrecognised.

A name that differs from another by one character can pass the name comparison (the limit is a similarity of 0.85), and an employer written in short form in one document and in full in another is flagged.
That the employer pays the salary is judged by one word of the employer's name against the descriptions of salary credits on the statement. It is a heuristic and can be wrong in either direction.
An account number that is masked, or short, matches another by its visible end, which must be at least three characters.
A payslip dated outside every statement period submitted is reported as not compared, not as a conflict. A set of several months' statements looks the same.
The same software producing different kinds of document within ten minutes is noted, and it also happens for ordinary reasons (one office system issuing both).

The context rules use reference limits that are synthetic and illustrative (obligations up to half of declared income, documents up to 90 days old); they are not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest.
Thresholds are starting values and have not been tuned or evaluated yet.
Untrusted files are opened in the same process as the tool. Size, page and time limits apply, but there is no sandbox.
Handwriting, stamps and signatures are not analysed, and text other than printed English is not read.
assumptions: Dates are read day first (DD/MM/YYYY); a date that could be read another way is marked ambiguous and given a low confidence.
Amounts are in rupees, with lakh or western digit grouping.
A usable PDF text layer is taken as read; a page whose text layer is unusable is read by OCR instead.
Boxes are pixels of the page rendered at 200 dpi unless a page says otherwise; points are pixels x 72 / dpi.
Documents are synthetic or authorised for the purpose, and one case is analysed at a time on one machine.
